concerns.concern: Up and down states show comparable dwell times even though the Zeeman splitting (~3.5 meV) far exceeds k_BT (~0.39 meV). A mechanism that merely opens a relaxation channel should drive the atom into the ground state, so an energy source or level shift is missing from the explanation.
concerns.quote: The data therefore require a source of energy or a level shift that the authors do not discuss.

concerns.concern: The small Δf contrast appears only at or beyond point contact, where the adatom relaxes laterally. A spin-state-dependent difference in geometry or bond length could produce the same signal, so attribution to an exchange force is not established.
concerns.quote: Any spin-state-dependent difference in adsorption geometry, bond length or lateral relaxation would produce a Δf difference indistinguishable from an "exchange force".

concerns.concern: There is no control measurement with a non-magnetic tip showing the absence of bistability and contrast.
concerns.quote: Δf on Ho with a non-magnetic tip, showing no bistability and no contrast.

concerns.concern: There is no control in which the tip magnetization is reversed (e.g., field to −3 T) to show that the readout contrast inverts.
concerns.quote: Reversal of the tip magnetization (B → −3 T), showing inversion of the readout contrast.

concerns.concern: The Sader–Jarvis force inversion assumes a conservative, z-only force, which fails when the adatom moves laterally. The oscillation amplitude is also comparable to the feature size, so the claimed FM→AFM sign change may be an inversion artifact.
concerns.quote: The sign changes in F_MExFM between z = 0 and −0.1 nm are therefore susceptible to inversion artifacts.

concerns.concern: The up/down state labels and the sign interpretation rest on unverified assumptions: that the Co tip is superparamagnetic and aligned with the field, and the sign of the TMR.
concerns.quote: The ↑/↓ assignment rests on the assumption that the Co-cluster tip is superparamagnetic and aligned with +B, and on the sign of the TMR.

concerns.concern: Writing is stochastic and telegraphic, so choosing a target state requires read-verify feedback. No success probability or error rate is given, and only the rate, not the orientation, depends on z.
concerns.quote: The claim that "spin orientation… can be controlled by adjusting the tip–sample distance" is not supported.

concerns.concern: There is no demonstration that the same adatom, switched repeatedly over many cycles, gives reproducible state-specific Δf values across several adatoms and tips.
concerns.quote: A Δf readout for an adatom in the same state measured repeatedly after many switching cycles, showing reproducible state-specific values.

concerns.concern: The spin-dependent contrast is tiny relative to the background, noise-dominated over much of the range, and reported without error bars or repeat statistics.
concerns.quote: noise-dominated over much of the range, with no error bars or repeat statistics.

concerns.concern: The statement that bidirectional switching rules out exchange forces is unjustified, because a tip-induced exchange bias is fully compatible with bidirectional switching.
concerns.quote: Scenario (a) is an exchange-mediated mechanism that is fully compatible with bidirectional switching.

concerns.concern: The switching mechanism is assumed rather than tested. Up and down rates and occupancy versus z should be reported separately, along with dependence on field, temperature, amplitude and bias polarity.
concerns.quote: Determine the switching mechanism experimentally rather than by assumption.

concerns.concern: The point-charge crystal-field model uses formal charges and an unrelaxed geometry, and is not benchmarked against experimentally constrained crystal-field parameters for Ho/MgO.
concerns.quote: It is a bare point-charge model with formal ±2e charges and an unrelaxed geometry.

concerns.concern: The α-interpolation between C2v and C4v Hamiltonians is never linked to an actual displacement, tip height or DFT-relaxed structure.
concerns.quote: α is never connected to an actual displacement, a tip height, or a DFT-relaxed structure.

concerns.concern: The tip's own symmetry-breaking and hybridization effects at point contact are dismissed qualitatively. They should be estimated, e.g., with DFT or a hybridization model.
concerns.quote: This is qualitative. At point contact, hybridization with the tip can strongly modify the 5d/6s shell, the crystal field and the exchange field.

concerns.concern: The transition metric I₀₁ ignores energy-dependent spectral densities, Boltzmann factors, phonon density of states and the hyperfine interaction.
concerns.quote: The metric I₀₁ (Eq. S6) ignores energy-dependent spectral densities, Boltzmann factors, phonon DOS and the hyperfine interaction known to matter for Ho.

concerns.concern: Conductances of ~10⁻²G₀ at the writing distances imply currents up to ~nA, so the method is not current-free. The roles of current and bias are not disentangled.
concerns.quote: The method is therefore not "current-free". The roles of current and bias, including at exactly V = 0 and with reversed polarity, are not disentangled.

concerns.concern: The window between no switching and irreversible conversion of the adatom to the bridge site is not quantified. Neither the fraction of destructive attempts nor the number of adatoms and cycles tested is reported.
concerns.quote: The working window between "no switching" and "bit destroyed" is never quantified for any tip.

concerns.concern: The switching-rate fits rest on only ~3–5 points over ~10 pm. They are compared with current-induced switching measured with a different tip, bias and distance.
concerns.quote: the force-switching fits for tips 4 and 5 rest on ~3–5 points spanning ~10 pm.

concerns.concern: Negligible measured dissipation cannot exclude mechanical driving, since the energy needed to flip one spin per second is far below the detection limit.
concerns.quote: Negligible dissipation (Fig. S7e) also cannot exclude mechanical driving.

concerns.concern: Lateral localization of switching, which matters for bit density, is never measured. Rate maps versus lateral position or tests on closely spaced adatoms are missing.
concerns.quote: lateral localization (essential for bit density) is never measured.

concerns.concern: The energy-efficiency claims lack any estimate of energy per write and any comparison with current-pulse or ESR protocols.
concerns.quote: No estimate is given of the energy per write: mechanical work in contact, resonator drive power, or Joule heating at the reported currents.

concerns.concern: The claims about long coherence times and quantum-information relevance are unsupported by coherence measurements. Repeated metal-tip contact would likely degrade T₁/T₂.
concerns.quote: The forward-looking statements about long coherence times and quantum information are not supported by any coherence-relevant measurement.

concerns.concern: The novelty of the mechanism is overstated. The work is not positioned against exchange-force switching proposals, tip-exchange-bias control and AFM single-spin detection literature.
concerns.quote: the novelty of the *mechanism* is less established than claimed

concerns.concern: z = 0 is defined as point contact at G₀, yet the measured conductance there is ~10⁻²G₀. It is also unclear whether static or deconvolved conductance is used.
concerns.quote: This calls into question what "point contact" means across tips and figures.

concerns.concern: It is not stated whether the left adatom in Fig. 5 was switched by force or by current, which is critical for the force-based narrative.
concerns.quote: It is not stated how the left adatom in Fig. 5 was switched (by force or by current)

concerns.concern: Fig. S3c shows an unexplained minimum and kink, suggesting numerical or level-crossing artifacts. Its exponential trend is not mapped onto the measured z-dependence.
concerns.quote: Fig. S3c shows an unexplained minimum near α ≈ 0.1 and a kink near α ≈ 0.3, suggesting numerical or level-crossing artifacts.

concerns.concern: The switching distance varies strongly between tips (~0 to −140 pm), and no strategy such as standardized tip-apex characterization is discussed to reduce this variability.
concerns.quote: Discuss strategies to reduce tip-to-tip variability (Fig. S13), such as a standardized tip-apex characterization.

concerns.concern: The full z-dependence of the contrast should be shown with the same tip that was used for switching.
concerns.quote: Show the full z-dependence of the contrast with the same tip used for switching.

concerns.concern: The Fig. S13 axis appears to be mislabeled in nm instead of pm.
concerns.quote: the axis is labeled "nm", presumably pm

concerns.concern: Residual non-English annotations remain in Fig. 4 and Fig. S1.
concerns.quote: Residual non-English annotations appear in Fig. 4 and Fig. S1.

concerns.concern: Ag(001) and Ag(100) are used interchangeably and should be unified.
concerns.quote: Ag(001) and Ag(100) are used interchangeably.
